pk.context: 5 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: yellow, flat-faced, scored round tablet with beveled edges

tell: Its active metabolite, N-desmethyldiazepam, has a terminal half-life of up to 100 hours, against up to 48 for the parent drug.

clues.text: More than 90% is absorbed, though a moderate-fat meal delays and reduces absorption. It is 98% bound to plasma proteins and is cleared mainly by cytochrome P450 oxidation.
A colorless to light yellow crystalline compound, insoluble in water, with a molecular weight of 284.75.
Under an NDA, tablets come in 2, 5 and 10 mg strengths, supplied in bottles of 100.
The boxed warning covers opioid co-use, abuse, misuse and addiction, and dependence. Contraindicated in acute narrow-angle glaucoma; drowsiness and ataxia are the commonest reactions.
Anxiety disorders and short-term anxiety symptoms, acute alcohol withdrawal, and adjunctive treatment of muscle spasm and seizure disorders.
Potentiates the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA by binding a site on the GABA-A receptor.
The generic name begins with D and has eight letters.
